verdict.summary: Creating and connecting your own Linear OAuth app is quick, and the docs document no account-type prerequisite or review for private use. The harder parts are token refresh (access tokens last 24 hours) and workspace-level approval settings that can block other workspaces from installing; directory listing is manual and has no documented timeline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for a private app with token refresh; add time for public distribution and any directory submission
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 15-30 minutes once you have a client ID and secret (estimate)
verdict.approval_wait: None documented for a private app or for public distribution; directory acceptance has no stated timeline

gates.name: Private app, your own workspace
gates.unlocks: Your own account can install and use the app in the workspace where you created it. Good for building and testing.
limits: Distribution defaults to private, meaning installable only in the current workspace.
Access tokens are valid for 24 hours and must be refreshed with the refresh token.
Linear recommends a separate workspace to manage the app, because every admin of that workspace gets access to it.

gates.name: Public distribution (cross-workspace install, no directory listing)
gates.unlocks: Other workspaces can install the app. The app does not appear in Linear's Integration Directory.
limits: Workspaces with third-party app review turned on make members request approval, and an admin must approve.
OAuth app rate limit is 5,000 requests per user (or app user) per hour and 2,000,000 complexity points per hour. Higher limits are granted case by case through Linear support.
No test-user allowlist or install cap is documented in the findings. Treat this gate as 'anyone who can get an admin to approve'.
gates.time_to_reach: Set distribution to public in the app form. No Linear review is documented. One community report says the app was available immediately.

gates.name: Integration Directory listing
gates.unlocks: Your app is listed in Linear's Integration Directory, where any Linear user can find it.
limits: Linear says it generally does not accept scripts, low-effort or vibe-coded apps, or hobbyist apps.
No privacy-policy, security-review or minimum-install requirement is documented.
Listing is separate from public distribution. You can have public distribution without a listing.
gates.time_to_reach: Not documented. Acceptance is manual and at Linear's discretion, with no stated timeline.

steps.title: Decide managed auth or your own app
steps.detail: Start on Composio's managed Linear auth config unless you need your own client ID/secret, your own redirect URI, a custom name or icon, public distribution, or actor=app. Composio's default scopes are read, write, issues:create and comments:create. Check them against what your integration needs.
gotchas: Composio's default scopes are Composio's choice, not Linear's.

steps.title: Create a separate admin workspace (recommended)
steps.detail: Linear recommends creating a dedicated workspace to manage the OAuth2 app. Every admin of that workspace can see and manage the app, so keep the admin list short.
gotchas: Admins of the workspace that owns the app get access to it.

steps.title: Open the OAuth application form
steps.detail: Sign in to the admin workspace and go to Settings, then API, then OAuth applications, or open the form directly at the URL below. Click to create a new OAuth2 application. Linear's docs list no account-type prerequisite (partner program, paid plan or business verification) for this step.
gotchas: If you use URL parameters or a JSON manifest, the form is pre-filled (see the manifest step).

steps.title: Fill in name, developer and client fields
steps.detail: Enter the application name and developer name. The client name must be 2-80 characters and must not contain the word 'Linear' or a URL scheme. Use a descriptive name for your integration.
gotchas: Manifest validation rejects a client name that contains 'Linear' or http:// or https://.

steps.title: Set the Redirect URI
steps.detail: In the redirect callback URL field of the OAuth application form, paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config. Linear checks redirect_uri on every authorize and token request, so it must match exactly.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Any mismatch in the URI, including a trailing slash, causes the authorize step to fail.
Only the redirect URIs you register here can be used.

steps.title: Choose distribution and optional client credentials
steps.detail: Leave distribution set to private for the first connection. Only turn on client credentials tokens if you need app-actor tokens. If you turn it on, you must do it when creating or editing the app.
gotchas: Client credentials tokens are app-actor tokens valid for 30 days, with up to 1000 active per app.

steps.title: Save credentials and enter them in Composio
steps.detail: Save the app and copy the client ID and client secret. In Composio, open the Linear auth config, choose your own app credentials, and paste the client ID and secret. You can rotate the secret later in Settings, then API without re-registering the app.
gotchas: Rotating the client secret does not revoke tokens already granted.

steps.title: Connect your own account
steps.detail: From Composio, connect a Linear account through the auth config. Your browser opens the Linear authorize page. Approve the requested scopes. Start with the minimum set you need, because each scope is shown to the user on the consent screen.
gotchas: Linear's authorize page returns 200 even for an invalid client_id, so a failed connection may show no error code. Check the client ID and secret first.

steps.title: Verify token exchange and refresh
steps.detail: An agent with access can check the token exchange: a form-encoded POST to the token URL with code, redirect_uri, client_id, client_secret and grant_type=authorization_code. Then confirm the access token expires in about 24 hours and that a refresh with the refresh token returns a new refresh token. Save the new refresh token each time.
gotchas: Refresh requests have a 30-minute grace period for network-error replays. Each refresh returns a new refresh token, so store it or the connection breaks.
All OAuth2 apps were migrated to the refresh-token system on April 1, 2026, so any older token logic that assumes long-lived tokens needs updating.

steps.title: Optional: PKCE or actor=app
steps.detail: PKCE is supported: add code_challenge and code_challenge_method (plain or S256) to the authorize request, and send code_verifier instead of client_secret in the token exchange. To make the app act as itself, not the authorizing user, add actor=app to the authorization URL. The user still authorizes installing the app in the workspace.
gotchas: Agent-specific scopes such as app:assignable and app:mentionable are documented on the Linear Agents page, not on the OAuth page. Their approval rules were not verified.

steps.title: Set public distribution for cross-workspace installs
steps.detail: In the app form, change distribution from private to public if other workspaces should be able to install the app. Public means installable by other workspaces. It does not list the app in the Integration Directory. Before you do this, check which target workspaces have third-party app review turned on.
gotchas: In workspaces with third-party app review on, members can only request approval. An admin must approve the app (on Enterprise, the workspace owner does this).

steps.title: Plan around rate limits
steps.detail: Design the integration to stay under 5,000 requests per user per hour and 2,000,000 complexity points per hour. Linear says it raises limits for workspace-level apps using actor authorization, based on paid users in the workspace. If you need more, ask Linear support, which reviews requests case by case.

values.label: Requests
values.value: 5,000 per user (or app user) per hour

steps.title: Draft the app manifest
steps.detail: An agent can draft a JSON manifest or URL parameters to pre-fill the creation form. Include developer.name, oauth.client_name, oauth.client_uri, at least one HTTPS or HTTP redirect URI (the Composio callback), and grant types. Any webhook URL must be HTTPS and must not point to loopback, private-network or linear.app hosts.

values.label: oauth.redirect_uris
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page); up to 32, unique

gotchas: Pre-filled URL parameters go to the workspace-agnostic version of the OAuth application creation form.

steps.title: Prepare directory assets and form
steps.detail: Fill out Linear's Integration Directory form. Send the icon and showcase assets to integrations@linear.app, or link them in the form. The docs list a 320px icon and a 1600x1000 showcase image. The form includes a sample page that shows the expected copy style and length.
gotchas: Linear generally does not accept scripts, low-effort or vibe-coded apps, or hobbyist apps. Describe your company and the value for users.

steps.title: Submit for directory review
steps.detail: Submit the form. Linear reviews it manually and accepts integrations it judges useful to the community and built by formal companies. The docs state no review timeline, minimum-install threshold or privacy-policy requirement.
gotchas: Directory acceptance is at Linear's discretion. Do not make launch depend on it.

steps.title: Wait for Linear's decision
steps.detail: Linear decides whether to list the app. No timeline is documented. Keep public distribution working in the meantime, since it does not depend on the directory listing.

The authorize and token requests must use a redirect_uri that matches a registered callback URL. The Composio callback URL is the one to register.

client_name must be 2-80 characters, must not contain 'Linear', and must not contain a URL scheme. developer.name must be 2-80 characters.

scopes.effect: Always present in Linear's scope model. Linear's docs do not classify it as sensitive or restricted. Composio includes it by default.
Needed for writes beyond creating issues and comments. Composio includes it by default. Request it only if your integration writes data.
Needed only if the integration creates issues.
Needed only if the integration posts comments.
Documented scope. Request it only if the integration writes time schedules.
Full access to admin-level endpoints. Linear's docs say never to ask for it unless it is absolutely needed. Expect scrutiny if you do.
Agent-specific scopes. Documented on the Linear Agents page, not on the OAuth page. Their approval rules were not verified.

blockers.symptom: Members of a target workspace see a request-approval prompt instead of an install.
blockers.cause: That workspace has third-party app review turned on, so installs need admin approval.
blockers.fix: Ask a workspace admin (the owner on Enterprise) to approve the app under Integrations and applications in Security. Do not assume public distribution means instant installs everywhere.

blockers.symptom: No decision on the Integration Directory submission.
blockers.cause: Directory acceptance is manual and discretionary. No review timeline is documented.
blockers.fix: Do not make launch depend on the listing. Public distribution works without it. Follow up through integrations@linear.app if needed.

blockers.symptom: The connection stops working after about 24 hours.
blockers.cause: Access tokens expire in 24 hours. Refresh tokens rotate on each refresh.
blockers.fix: Implement a refresh step that stores the new refresh token every time. Use the 30-minute grace period only for replays after network errors.

blockers.symptom: Manifest or app form rejects the client name.
blockers.cause: The client name contains 'Linear' or a URL scheme, or is outside 2-80 characters.
blockers.fix: Rename the app to a 2-80 character name without 'Linear' and without http:// or https://.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Linear auth config. Create your own Linear OAuth app only if you need your own client_id/secret, your own redirect URI, a custom app name or icon, public distribution to other workspaces, or client_credentials / actor=app. Composio's default scopes are its own choice, not Linear's: read is always present in Linear's model, and write is broader than most read-only integrations need. Check the scope list before you go live.

open_questions: No documented Linear review gate for publishing an OAuth app to other workspaces. Directory acceptance is manual and discretionary, with no stated timeline, privacy-policy, security-review, logo or minimum-install requirement. No list of rejection reasons was found.

No test-user allowlist, install cap or dev-store equivalent is documented for Linear. Gate 2 is therefore modeled as public distribution only, and the findings do not confirm a limited-audience stage.
The single report that public apps were available immediately (f23) is not a documented rule. Confirm with Linear before relying on it.
Whether third-party app review is on by default and whether it exists on every paid plan comes from one community guide and is not checked against Linear's official docs.
The Agents page and Agent Interaction Guidelines were not fetched in full. app:assignable, app:mentionable and their approval rules are unverified.
Composio's managed Linear app may request scopes beyond its default list. This was not verified.
Linear's authorize endpoint returns 200 for an invalid client_id, so how an invalid client is rejected at the token step is unverified. No real client ID was created.
The docs do not classify any Linear scope as sensitive or restricted. Whether read alone is sufficient depends on the features an integration uses.
